Bug_Title: Classes should not access their own subclasses during class initialization
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by having the static variable 'field1' in the 'ClassInitializationBug' class initialized with a call to a static method'method()' in the subclass 'Child'. This creates a dependency on the order of class initialization and can lead to unexpected behavior.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method, which relies on the static initialization of ClassInitializationBug. During this initialization, it calls Child.method(), which in turn references Parent.field2. This creates a dependency on the order of class initialization, leading to unexpected behavior where field1 is initialized to 0 instead of 42.
